@@ -0,0 +1,388 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Generate the paper's accuracy figures from the repeated-AE campaign data.
+
+Two figures, matching the style of the existing paper plots:
+
+  fig-heap-accesses.pdf   ratio of ZRay-reported to Pin-reported heap access
+                          volume, in bytes read and bytes written
+
+Byte volume, not load/store instruction counts, is what carries the accuracy
+claim: the instruction counts have separate inaccuracies of their own that would
+confound this comparison. The counts can still be plotted with --with-counts,
+which writes a second figure alongside.
+
+Both put GAPBS and SPEC on one axis with a geometric mean at the right, the same
+layout the previous figures used. Colors, bar geometry, and the DejaVu Sans face
+are taken from those PDFs so these drop in beside them.
+
+Usage:
+  ./make-figures.py                       # tripcount build, paper's GAPBS subset
+  ./make-figures.py --build postfix       # the pre-loop-fix build
+  ./make-figures.py --all-gapbs           # include cc_sv and pr_spmv too
+  ./make-figures.py --errorbars           # draw +/-1 SEM caps
+  ./make-figures.py --with-counts         # also plot load/store instruction counts
+  ./make-figures.py --rate                # bandwidth-accuracy figure instead
+
+A workload whose reference is zero (no writes in its region) has no ratio and is
+drawn as an empty slot labelled N/A, rather than as a bar at 1.0.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import math
+import os
+import statistics as st
+
+import matplotlib
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import numpy as np
+from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
+from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator
+from matplotlib.patches import Patch
+
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+
+# Sampled from the existing figures: plum and indigo, with the second series
+# hatched so the pair survives greyscale printing.
+C_FIRST, C_SECOND = "#DDA0DD", "#4B0082"
+HATCH_SECOND = "//"
+# The unity line is the reference every bar is read against, so it is black and
+# heavier than the suite separators, which stay red and thinner.
+C_UNITY = "black"
+C_SPLIT = "red"
+# Workloads with no reference to divide by. Kept deliberately quiet: the bar has
+# to span the plot so the slot cannot be misread as a ratio of zero, but it is not
+# a result and should not compete with the data for attention.
+C_NA_FACE = "#E4E4E6"
+C_NA_EDGE = "#B4B4BA"
+HATCH_NA = "///"
+
+# Third series, for the sampling figure only. Light-to-dark tracks sparse-to-dense
+# sampling, so the visual order matches the meaning without needing the legend.
+C_MID = "#9370DB"
+HATCH_MID = "xx"
+
+# Sampling rates, plotted in this order: sparsest first, every-ROI last.
+SAMPLE_RATES = [(100, "1 in 100 ROI"), (10, "1 in 10 ROI"), (1, "Every ROI")]
+
+GAPBS_PAPER = ["bc", "bfs", "cc", "pr", "sssp", "tc"]
+GAPBS_ALL = ["bc", "bfs", "cc", "cc_sv", "pr", "pr_spmv", "sssp", "tc"]
+SPEC = ["perlbench", "gcc", "mcf", "namd", "parest", "povray", "lbm", "omnetpp",
+        "xalancbmk", "x264", "blender", "deepsjeng", "imagick", "leela", "nab", "xz"]
+
+# Which aggregated CSV holds each build. The GAPBS post-fix campaign predates the
+# variant-scoped naming, so it has no infix.
+SOURCES = {
+    "tripcount": ("gapbs-tripcount-reps-accuracy.csv", "spec-tripcount-reps-accuracy.csv"),
+    "postfix":   ("gapbs-reps-accuracy.csv", None),
+}
+
+# Bandwidth accuracy. ZRay's side is its reported LOAD/WRITE BW, which already
+# carries the runtime's counter-overhead correction factor; the control is Pin's
+# bytes over the ROI time from the timing-only build. Source is rate-accuracy.csv,
+# written by compute-rates.py -- a single run, so no error bars.
+FIG_RATE = dict(out="fig-bandwidth-accuracy.pdf",
+                metrics=("read", "write"),
+                labels=("Read", "Write"),
+                title="Data Volume Rate Accuracy",
+                ylabel="Ratio ZRay:Control",
+                source="rate")
+
+FIG_BYTES = dict(out="fig-heap-accesses.pdf",
+                 metrics=("read B", "write B"),
+                 labels=("Bytes read", "Bytes written"),
+                 title="ZRay Heap Byte Access Accuracy",
+                 ylabel="Ratio ZRay:Baseline",
+                 source="accuracy")
+
+# Secondary, off by default: the instruction counts carry inaccuracies unrelated
+# to what this figure is about.
+FIG_COUNTS = dict(out="fig-access-counts.pdf",
+                  metrics=("loads", "stores"),
+                  labels=("Loads", "Stores"),
+                  title="ZRay Heap Access Count Accuracy",
+                  ylabel="Ratio ZRay:Baseline",
+                  source="accuracy")
+
+
+def load_rates(suite):
+    """Bandwidth ratios from compute-rates.py, in the same shape as load()."""
+    out = {}
+    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "rate-accuracy.csv")) as fh:
+        for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
+            if r["suite"] != suite:
+                continue
+            v = float(r["ratio"]) if r["ratio"] else None
+            out[(r["workload"], r["metric"])] = [v]
+    return out
+
+
+def load_sampling(suite):
+    """{workload: {rate: slowdown}} from the sampling sweep.
+
+    Each rate is divided by its own contemporaneous control -- run-spec.sh and
+    collect-gapbs.sh run the uninstrumented build back to back with the ZRay one
+    -- so machine drift between the three passes cannot show up as a sampling
+    effect. Single run per rate, so there are no error bars.
+    """
+    fname = "spec-zray-stats.csv" if suite == "spec" else "zray-gapbs-stats.csv"
+    out = {}
+    for rate, _ in SAMPLE_RATES:
+        path = os.path.join(ROOT, "results-sampling", f"rate-{rate}", fname)
+        if not os.path.exists(path):
+            continue
+        with open(path) as fh:
+            for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
+                try:
+                    t = float(r["Elapsed Real Time"])
+                    b = float(r["Baseline Elapsed Real Time"])
+                except (KeyError, ValueError):
+                    continue
+                if b:
+                    out.setdefault(r["Name"], {})[rate] = t / b
+    return out
+
+
+def load(path):
+    """Return {(workload, metric): [ratio per rep]}, with None where undefined."""
+    out = {}
+    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, path)) as fh:
+        for r in csv.DictReader(fh):
+            z, p = int(r["zray"]), int(r["pin"])
+            out.setdefault((r["workload"], r["metric"]), []).append(z / p if p else None)
+    return out
+
+
+def agg(values):
+    v = [x for x in values if x is not None]
+    if not v:
+        return None
+    return (st.mean(v), (st.stdev(v) / len(v) ** 0.5) if len(v) > 1 else 0.0)
+
+
+def build_series(data, workloads, metric):
+    """Per-workload (mean, sem), plus the geometric mean over the defined ones."""
+    pts = [agg(data.get((w, metric), [])) for w in workloads]
+    defined = [p[0] for p in pts if p]
+    gmean = math.exp(st.mean([math.log(x) for x in defined])) if defined else None
+    return pts, gmean
+
+
+def draw_sampling(args, gk):
+    """Runtime overhead against ROI sampling rate. Lower is better; 1 = none."""
+    from matplotlib.ticker import LogLocator, ScalarFormatter, NullFormatter
+
+    gapbs, spec = load_sampling("gapbs"), load_sampling("spec")
+    if not gapbs and not spec:
+        print("no sampling data under results-sampling/; skipping")
+        return
+    sk = [w for w in SPEC if w in spec]
+    gk = [w for w in gk if w in gapbs]
+    names = gk + sk + ["geomean"]
+
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(0.30 * len(names) + 1.0, 4.1))
+    x = np.arange(len(names), dtype=float)
+    width = 0.26
+
+    styles = [(C_FIRST, None), (C_MID, HATCH_MID), (C_SECOND, HATCH_SECOND)]
+    for i, ((rate, label), (color, hatch)) in enumerate(zip(SAMPLE_RATES, styles)):
+        vals = [gapbs.get(w, {}).get(rate) for w in gk] + \
+               [spec.get(w, {}).get(rate) for w in sk]
+        defined = [v for v in vals if v]
+        vals.append(math.exp(st.mean([math.log(v) for v in defined])) if defined else None)
+        off = (i - 1) * width
+        for xi, v in zip(x, vals):
+            if v is None:
+                continue
+            ax.bar(xi + off, v, width, color=color, hatch=hatch,
+                   edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.7, zorder=3)
+
+    # Log scale by default: gcc runs 16x while most workloads sit between 1.0x and
+    # 2.0x, and on a linear axis that single bar flattens every other difference
+    # in the figure into invisibility. --linear draws the comparison.
+    if args.linear:
+        top = max([v for w in list(gapbs.values()) + list(spec.values())
+                   for v in w.values()] + [1.0])
+        ax.set_ylim(0, top * 1.06)
+        ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(1.0))
+    else:
+        ax.set_yscale("log")
+        ax.set_ylim(0.9, 22)
+        ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(LogLocator(base=10, subs=(1.0, 2.0, 5.0), numticks=12))
+        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(ScalarFormatter())
+        ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(NullFormatter())
+    ax.axhline(1.0, color=C_UNITY, linewidth=2.0, linestyle="--", zorder=2)
+    if sk:
+        ax.axvline(len(gk) - 0.5, color=C_SPLIT, linewidth=1.4, linestyle="--", zorder=2)
+    ax.axvline(len(names) - 1.5, color=C_SPLIT, linewidth=1.4, linestyle="--", zorder=2)
+
+    ax.set_xlim(-0.58, len(names) - 0.42)
+    ax.set_xticks(x)
+    ax.set_xticklabels(names, rotation=90, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=14)
+    ax.set_xlabel("Workload", fontsize=12)
+    ax.set_ylabel("Runtime vs. uninstrumented")
+    ax.set_title("ZRay Runtime Overhead by Sampling Rate", pad=26, fontsize=13.5)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(False)
+    ax.yaxis.grid(True, which="major", linestyle=":", linewidth=0.7,
+                  color="0.35", alpha=0.45, zorder=3.5)
+
+    handles = [Patch(facecolor=c, edgecolor="black", hatch=h, label=lbl)
+               for (_, lbl), (c, h) in zip(SAMPLE_RATES, styles)]
+    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, 1.005, 1, 0.1),
+              mode="expand", ncol=3, frameon=False, fontsize=10.5,
+              handlelength=1.4, handletextpad=0.5, columnspacing=1.0, borderaxespad=0)
+
+    stem = "fig-sampling-overhead" + ("-linear" if args.linear else "")
+    out = os.path.join(args.outdir, stem + ".pdf")
+    fig.savefig(out, bbox_inches="tight")
+    fig.savefig(out.replace(".pdf", ".png"), dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+    print(f"wrote {out}")
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--build", default="tripcount", choices=sorted(SOURCES))
+    ap.add_argument("--all-gapbs", action="store_true",
+                    help="include cc_sv and pr_spmv, which the paper figures omit")
+    ap.add_argument("--errorbars", action="store_true", help="draw ±1 SEM caps")
+    ap.add_argument("--with-counts", action="store_true",
+                    help="also plot load/store instruction counts")
+    ap.add_argument("--rate", action="store_true",
+                    help="plot bandwidth accuracy instead of byte volume")
+    ap.add_argument("--sampling", action="store_true",
+                    help="plot runtime overhead by ROI sampling rate")
+    ap.add_argument("--linear", action="store_true",
+                    help="sampling figure: linear y-axis instead of log")
+    ap.add_argument("--outdir", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "figures"))
+    args = ap.parse_args()
+
+    os.makedirs(args.outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    plt.rcParams.update({
+        "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
+        "font.size": 13,
+        "axes.linewidth": 1.0,
+        "xtick.major.pad": 2,
+        "ytick.major.pad": 2,
+        "axes.labelpad": 3,
+        "pdf.fonttype": 42,
+    })
+    if args.sampling:
+        draw_sampling(args, GAPBS_ALL if args.all_gapbs else GAPBS_PAPER)
+        return
+
+    gapbs_csv, spec_csv = SOURCES[args.build]
+    if args.rate:
+        gapbs, spec = load_rates("gapbs"), load_rates("spec")
+    else:
+        gapbs = load(gapbs_csv)
+        spec = load(spec_csv) if spec_csv else {}
+    if not spec:
+        print(f"note: no SPEC data for build '{args.build}'; plotting GAPBS only")
+
+    gk = GAPBS_ALL if args.all_gapbs else GAPBS_PAPER
+    sk = SPEC if spec else []
+    names = gk + sk + ["geomean"]
+    os.makedirs(args.outdir, exist_ok=True)
+
+    plt.rcParams.update({
+        "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",
+        "font.size": 13,
+        "axes.linewidth": 1.0,
+        "xtick.major.pad": 2,
+        "ytick.major.pad": 2,
+        "axes.labelpad": 3,
+        "pdf.fonttype": 42,          # embed as TrueType, not Type 3
+    })
+
+    figures = ([FIG_RATE] if args.rate
+               else [FIG_BYTES] + ([FIG_COUNTS] if args.with_counts else []))
+    for spec_fig in figures:
+        m1, m2 = spec_fig["metrics"]
+        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(0.26 * len(names) + 1.0, 4.1))
+
+        series = []
+        for metric in (m1, m2):
+            gp, gg = build_series(gapbs, gk, metric)
+            sp, sg = build_series(spec, sk, metric) if sk else ([], None)
+            pts = gp + sp
+            allv = [p[0] for p in pts if p]
+            overall = math.exp(st.mean([math.log(v) for v in allv])) if allv else None
+            series.append(pts + [(overall, 0.0)])
+
+        x = np.arange(len(names), dtype=float)
+        width = 0.36
+
+        # The y limit has to be known before drawing, because an undefined slot is
+        # drawn as a full-height bar rather than as a gap.
+        top = max([p[0] for s in series for p in s if p] + [1.0])
+        ylim = max(1.12, top * 1.06)
+
+        for i, (pts, color, hatch, label) in enumerate([
+                (series[0], C_FIRST, None, spec_fig["labels"][0]),
+                (series[1], C_SECOND, HATCH_SECOND, spec_fig["labels"][1])]):
+            off = (i - 0.5) * width
+            for xi, p in zip(x, pts):
+                if p is None:
+                    # No reference to divide by. A full-height hazard bar reads as
+                    # "no measurement" at a glance, where an empty slot could be
+                    # mistaken for a ratio of zero.
+                    ax.bar(xi + off, ylim, width, color=C_NA_FACE, hatch=HATCH_NA,
+                           edgecolor=C_NA_EDGE, linewidth=0.6, zorder=1)
+                    continue
+                ax.bar(xi + off, p[0], width, color=color, hatch=hatch,
+                       edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.7, zorder=3)
+                if args.errorbars and p[1] > 0:
+                    ax.errorbar(xi + off, p[0], yerr=p[1], fmt="none",
+                                ecolor="black", elinewidth=1.1, capsize=3, zorder=4)
+
+        ax.axhline(1.0, color=C_UNITY, linewidth=2.0, linestyle="--", zorder=2)
+        if sk:
+            # Suite boundary, and the geomean set apart from both.
+            ax.axvline(len(gk) - 0.5, color=C_SPLIT, linewidth=1.4,
+                       linestyle="--", zorder=2)
+        ax.axvline(len(names) - 1.5, color=C_SPLIT, linewidth=1.4,
+                   linestyle="--", zorder=2)
+
+        ax.set_ylim(0, ylim)
+        ax.set_xlim(-0.58, len(names) - 0.42)
+        ax.set_xticks(x)
+        ax.set_xticklabels(names, rotation=90, ha="center", va="top", fontsize=14)
+        ax.set_xlabel("Workload", fontsize=12)
+        ax.set_ylabel(spec_fig["ylabel"])
+        ax.set_title(spec_fig["title"], pad=26, fontsize=13.5)
+        # Auto ticks go to 0.5 steps once the axes are this short, which is too
+        # coarse to read a ratio against; hold them at 0.25.
+        ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(0.25))
+        # Grid rides *over* the bars so a value can be read off the figure
+        # without tracing back to the axis. Alpha keeps it from competing with
+        # the bar fills; zorder 3.5 puts it above the bars (3) but below the
+        # error bars (4), which have to stay crisp.
+        ax.set_axisbelow(False)
+        ax.yaxis.grid(True, linestyle=":", linewidth=0.7, color="0.35",
+                      alpha=0.45, zorder=3.5)
+
+        handles = [Patch(facecolor=C_FIRST, edgecolor="black", label=spec_fig["labels"][0]),
+                   Patch(facecolor=C_SECOND, edgecolor="black", hatch=HATCH_SECOND,
+                         label=spec_fig["labels"][1]),
+                   Patch(facecolor=C_NA_FACE, edgecolor=C_NA_EDGE, hatch=HATCH_NA,
+                         label="No reference")]
+        # Above the axes, not inside them: the no-reference bars run the full
+        # height of the plot, so there is no longer any interior region a legend
+        # can occupy without covering data.
+        ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="lower left", bbox_to_anchor=(0, 1.005, 1, 0.1),
+                  mode="expand", ncol=3, frameon=False, fontsize=10.5,
+                  borderaxespad=0, handlelength=1.6, handletextpad=0.5,
+                  columnspacing=1.4)
+
+        fig.tight_layout(pad=0.25)
+        path = os.path.join(args.outdir, spec_fig["out"])
+        fig.savefig(path)
+        fig.savefig(path.replace(".pdf", ".png"), dpi=150)
+        plt.close(fig)
+        print(f"wrote {path}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
